title: Prove an exact Gaussian boundary determinant and rank obstruction (no κ)
body:
## Summary

A scoped mathematical proof gives the exact cross-rim determinant after eliminating a contiguous interior of a truncated Gaussian:

```text
bandwidth b, interior length m>=b, nonzero t, invertible interior A
    det C = (-1)^(bm) t^(b^2(m+b)) / det A
    rank C = b
    every exact factorization C=UV through k scalars has k>=b
```

The formula holds over every field. A more general outer-band product identity and covariance under nonzero diagonal gauges are proved in `research/gaussian-cross-rim-determinant/PROOF.md`. The exact rational fixture b=2, m=3, t=1/2 has det A=135/256 and det C=1/552960.

The new result is the exact determinant, including parameters and fields outside the older real positivity range. Full-rank consequences in 0<t<=1/3 already follow from Nick Petalas's PR5207 ordered-minor theorem and remain credited to it. The triangular-minor and block-determinant identities are classical; no general literature-priority claim is made. This is an original boundary question, not a predecessor audit. No new kappa or selected-frontier change is claimed.

## Evidence

Earlier bandwidth/support and restricted sign results do not provide this exact determinant. The new direct rational Schur construction and fraction-free host-minor calculation agree in every one of 144 Gaussian, 20 asymmetric banded and 12 signed-gauge cases. Eight invalid inputs reject and three semantic counterexamples pass. The all-size and arbitrary-field claims rest on the written proof; the finite checker runs over Q.

Local CPython 3.12.15 on macOS passes both registered commands, with identical normal/optimized receipts. Individually timed commands take 0.1033 and 0.1041 seconds locally, below their 120-second limits. Generated stdout receipts bind all six package-file hashes. AST/function-size inspection passes, with maximum function length 29 lines. Committed bytes and declared source ancestry pass at `9bb6afaa2b8f6c837bd6ff407e365fdae6382e7e`.

Exact reproduction from the repository root:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/gaussian-cross-rim-determinant/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -O -B research/gaussian-cross-rim-determinant/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/gaussian-cross-rim-determinant
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/gaussian-cross-rim-determinant --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_GAUSSIAN_CROSS_RIM_DETERMINANT`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Substitute another CPython 3.12 path if needed. No third-party dependencies, network access or predecessor executable is required by the standalone verifier. The selected metadata orientation separately passes.

## Limitations

This only rules out an exact linear factorization of the entire cross-rim map through fewer than b scalar channels. It does not bound recursive calls, machine instructions or an implementation retaining other cross-rim paths. Approximate rank and low displacement rank remain possible. The caller already allows O(b) boundary width, so its asymptotic cost is unchanged.

Actual caller/kernel/truncation admission, useful singular-value bounds, rounded error propagation, native/physical costs and all five framework assumptions remain open. No predecessor scientific replay, selected cold replay, finite-field census, Lean, Docker, independent human review or formal proof-kernel acceptance ran. The arbitrary-field argument is written, not a claimed exhaustive computation.

## Open next questions

Can approximate cross-rim compression improve one actual retained solve's complete paid bill? First pin the literal kernel, truncation, gauges and allowed final error, then prove a singular-value tail bound and charge representation, movement and error propagation. Exact full rank alone does not decide this. Research stopped at the first verified formula.

## Related open work

- [PR1754](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1754) proposes structured boundary solves using displacement rank. The ordinary cross-rim rank proved here does not exclude that representation or audit its cost.
- [PR1758](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1758) adds shifted/gauged Gaussian interiors to those structured solves. This proof preserves exact rank under nonzero diagonal gauges and does not check the proposed numerical implementation.
- [PR371](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/371) accounts for final-grid Gaussian rounding. This exact determinant does not estimate rounded errors or alter that result.
- [PR3910](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3910) proves a physical Gaussian row-norm transfer bound for a different local contract. No row-norm quantity is computed or compared here.

- [PR6405](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/6405) determines the sharp uniform real range 0<t<=1/2 for ordered minors and Schur-fill signs of the same truncated kernel. This PR gives the exact cross-rim determinant over every field, conditional on interior nonsingularity. No shared determinant value is computed by PR6405, and no extra comparison computation was run.
